headline: Third Mattress Store Opens on Block With Zero Foot Traffic, Fueling 'Mattress Dimension' Theory
subheadline: New location directly across from Hartwell Building; conspiracy theorists connect the dots
summary: The opening of yet another mattress store in a seemingly unprofitable location has reignited theories about what these businesses actually do.
content:
SleepWell Mattress Emporium has opened its newest location at 847 Hartwell Avenue—directly across from the Hartwell Building—becoming the third mattress store on a block that residents describe as "aggressively empty at all times."

The opening has reignited the "Mattress Dimension Theory," a long-running internet conspiracy claiming that mattress stores are not actually retail establishments but rather portals to an alternate dimension composed entirely of mattresses.

"Look at the economics," explained theory proponent @MattressSkeptic on Threadit. "There are four mattress stores within three blocks of each other. None of them ever have customers. But they've been open for 15 years. Where is the money coming from? It's not coming from mattresses. It's coming from The Dimension."

The theory suggests that mattress stores serve as "soft entry points" between our reality and a parallel dimension. Believers claim the stores' perpetually empty showrooms are actually staffed by "dimensional travelers" who use the mattresses as vessels.

"Why do you think they're always having sales?" @MattressSkeptic continued. "They don't care about profit. They're harvesting something else. Sleep energy. Dream data. Something."

SleepWell's spokesperson, who gave their name only as "Steve," dismissed the theories. "We sell mattresses," Steve said. "People need mattresses. We provide mattresses. That's all." When asked how many mattresses the new location had sold since opening two months ago, Steve said "several" and ended the interview.

The proximity to the Hartwell Building has not escaped notice. "Floor 13 doesn't exist," noted @HartwellSecrets. "And there's a mattress store across the street. What if Floor 13 is in the mattresses?"

Omnicorp Holdings, which owns both the Hartwell Building and the block's commercial properties, declined to comment.

At press time, a fourth mattress store had applied for permits on the same block.
author: Sandra Mitchell, Local News
